I'm 62 this year, been farming these 16 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. Just me and my wife now — our children work in Shijiazhuang and only come back for Spring Festival. We're getting older, and the heavy work gets harder every year. I've organized my land so that 14.1 mu is in wheat-maize double cropping, which I can mostly manage with the tractor and hired combine. I keep 2 mu of cotton because the price was decent last year and my neighbor Lao Zhang always does well with it, but honestly, picking is getting difficult for my back.

The wheat went in last October — I used an improved *Jimai* variety, bought certified seed from the supply shop because my saved seed was losing vigor. I put down base fertilizer then: about 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. Now it's early spring, and the wheat is waking up. I'll topdress with urea at green-up — about 15 kg per mu. The extension agent recommended 18 kg, but urea is up to 2.6 yuan per jin this year, and I need to watch my cash. I'll irrigate three times: once now as it warms, once at jointing, and once at heading if the weather turns dry. Pumping from the well costs about 20 yuan each time per mu, so every irrigation is a decision.

For maize, I'll plant immediately after the wheat harvest in early June. I hire a combine to cut the wheat — 50 yuan per mu — then I have less than a week to get the maize in the ground before the soil dries. I buy hybrid seed from the shop in town, about 45 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the planting furrow, roughly 25 kg per mu, then I'll topdress with urea at the big trumpet stage if the leaves look yellow. One or two irrigations for maize, usually just one at tasseling if there's no rain. My nephew sometimes helps with the planting, but otherwise it's just us.

Cotton — I'm planting 2 mu in mid-April. I use plastic mulch, it's the only way to get good emergence here. Base fertilizer is DAP, about 12 kg per mu. Then I topdress twice: 8 kg urea at budding and another 5 kg at flowering. The bollworm is my biggest worry — I spray three times for insects, plus a herbicide before laying the mulch. I irrigate twice, at flowering and during boll filling. For picking, I have to hire labor now — about 6 days at 100 yuan per day. My wife and I can handle the early picks, but the main harvest is too much bending for us. It's expensive, but if the lint price stays above 7 yuan per jin, it should pay.

I'm looking at about 8,500 yuan in total input costs this year. I have some cash left from selling last fall's maize, but I need to be careful — my wife's blood pressure medicine is a regular expense, and if we get a dry year, the pumping costs will eat into everything. I'm not trying to maximize anything; I'm just trying to get through the year with decent yields and not lose money.
